text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.95% today after oil prices dropped on news of diplomatic efforts to ease Saudi-Iran tensions. Yesterday and today brought reports of Saudi Arabia's defense minister meeting with Iran's president in Tehran, which reduced investor fears about potential disruptions to Middle Eastern oil production and exports — the opposite of the supply-shock concerns that had pushed crude up to six-month highs just days earlier. With crude now trading at $107.89 domestically and $115.22 globally, down from the $116+ peak on October 23rd, the immediate pressure driving energy stocks higher has eased.

The stock's 1.95% decline fits a reversal of a sharp four-day rally: COP jumped $5.17 (3.5%) between October 22nd and October 26th as Middle East tensions escalated, then gave back most of those gains today as de-escalation news shifted the outlook. Oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefit from higher prices, but they're also sensitive to what traders expect prices will do next — and today's diplomatic headlines signaled that the geopolitical risk premium that had lifted crude is fading.
